items.title: Web Search on AWS Bedrock now supports domain filtering and user location controls
items.content_snippet: Web Search on AWS Bedrock now supports two new controls that give you more precision over the results that ground a model's response: domain filtering and user location. Both are configured directly on the web_search tool in your existing OpenAI Responses API request. With domain filtering, you can restrict Web Search results to a set of domains you choose. items.content_snippet: Amazon Connect Customer Global Resiliency now provides customers a mechanism to deliver long, persistent chat experiences across linked AWS Regions. items.title: AWS Transit Gateway and AWS Cloud WAN now support 1:1 NAT
items.content_snippet: AWS Transit Gateway and AWS Cloud WAN now provide managed one-to-one network address translation (NAT) directly on their attachments, through integration with Regional Private NAT Gateway. items.title: How Shield uses OpenAI’s Astra to support IT teams
items.content_snippet: When someone can’t log in or get online, their IT team often has to put other work on hold. Shield is building Forge to help IT services teams get their customers back to work faster. Its AI agents use Astra to work directly in business software and resolve problems that previously needed a technician. items.title: How AT&T is building AI-powered legal workflows with OpenAI
items.content_snippet: AT&T’s David McAtee and Bill Ryan describe how AI is changing their legal team’s work—and what they plan to build with OpenAI next. One initiative is a natural-language intake system that would classify and prioritize legal matters, then connect them with relevant knowledge. The aim is to put better information in lawyers’ hands and give them more time for strategy and judgment. Decision-making remains with the lawyers.

items.title: From analyst to builder with Codex | Benefit Street Partners
items.content_snippet: Anant Kumar at Benefit Street Partners used Codex to build a tool that collects loan valuations from SEC filings and turns them into a website with visualizations. The first version took about a day. “I’ve gone from being just an analyst and a portfolio manager to being a developer as well now. I can build things.”

items.title: How Benefit Street Partners is building financial analysis tools with Codex
items.content_snippet: “I’ve gone from being just an analyst and a portfolio manager to being a developer as well now. I can build things.” Benefit Street Partners’ Anant Kumar wanted to compare how firms valued the same loans. The information was spread across SEC filings. He built a tool to collect it automatically and turn it into a website with visualizations. The first version took about a day. He calls Codex the big unlock. Watch how building his own tools changed the speed and depth of his analysis.

items.title: Can AI Understand a Distressed Credit? - Harneet Kaur, Axim Intelligence
items.content_snippet: Harneet Kaur, founder and CEO of Axim Intelligence and a former distressed credit investor, tests whether frontier models can reason about a live distressed situation: iHeartMedia. Given the same context, two top models disagreed sharply on the odds of bankruptcy versus a negotiated restructuring. Breaking the analysis into checked layers (extraction, derivation, judgment, prediction) brought them to the same answer, which raises a new question: is agreement the same as being right? items.title: Proving Alpha: How a Hedge Fund Measures AI's ROI - Hari Kumar, Contour Asset Management
items.content_snippet: Hari Kumar, head of AI at Contour Asset Management, a $6B fundamental long/short fund focused on tech, media and telecom, tackles the hardest question in AI adoption: what are we actually getting for the spend? He shares how Contour runs live A/B tests of analysts' research with and without AI tools, tracks "cost per useful insight," uses agents to resurface old ideas when the market makes them interesting again, and extends the same thinking to trading, ops and compliance. items.title: Buying GPUs Should Work Like Buying Stocks — Carmen Li, Compute Exchange

Compute Exchange is a neutral marketplace that owns no GPUs, verifies both providers and buyers, and handles reserved and forward contracts for GPUs and tokens, plus a busy market for used servers.
